next_step: Network topology workshop with Elmbridge infra + security whitepaper handoff (scheduled 2026-03-12)
notes: Initial qualification: regulated EU financial services firm, sensitive PII and transaction data, strong preference for in-region processing (EU-only).
Profile: global trading platform, 1200 employees, existing multi-account AWS footprint (eu-west-1 primary, eu-central-1 DR).
Primary ask: Private VPC deployment (customer-managed VPC) with optional on-prem connective path for air-gapped analytics cluster later in roadmap.

Workload: chat-based agent for trading desk support + document search across regulatory filings + reranking of trade alerts. Latency target: median <250ms for short-chat loops; p95 <700ms. Throughput target: 600 req/min with burst to 2k.
Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay premium for residency & audit controls but expect Redwood Optimize suggestions for quantization/batching to manage unit costs.

Security posture: Okta SSO/SAML mandatory, SCIM provisioning, enterprise SIEM integration, SOC2 + ISO27001 required. Elmbridge will run a vendor security questionnaire and expects encrypted audit logs forwarded to their logging account.

KMS: customer wants Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) in their AWS account (HSM-backed). Requirement: Redwood supports envelope encryption with customer KMS, key rotation policy, and key usage audit trail. Also asked about bringing HSM/CloudHSM options and KMS cross-account IAM role patterns.

Audit logging & retention: full request/response metadata (no sensitive prompt text persisted by default) to be logged; retention controls configurable per legal team — initial ask 13 months. Logs must be exportable to their S3 bucket and forwarded to Splunk/Datadog.

Data residency: strict EU residency for inference and logs. POC should run in eu-west-1. Discussed fallback policy: Redwood can failover to compatible model variant in same region; cross-region fallback requires legal approval.

Network topology preferences discussed: private endpoints (PrivateLink) or VPC Peering + Transit Gateway. Elmbridge ops prefers PrivateLink with customer VPC endpoints for least blast radius; open to Transit Gateway for multi-account scale.

Inbound/outbound rules: Elmbridge will not allow inbound access into their VPC from Redwood. Preferred model: Redwood workers in customer VPC (hosted daemon) or Redwood-managed VPC with customer peering where outbound goes to Redwood endpoints. Need clarification on whether Redwood requires NAT egress and which IP ranges/FQDNs to whitelist.

Suggested architecture options reviewed during call: 1) Redwood-hosted control plane + customer data plane in Elmbridge VPC (recommended); 2) Fully customer-deployed on-prem package (phase 2); 3) Dedicated reserved capacity in Elmbridge's cloud account. Team leaning toward option 1 for fastest time-to-value.

TLS / network auth: Elmbridge requires mTLS for control-plane to data-plane communication and client cert pinned for admin operations. Also asked about OIDC for service-to-service auth and short-lived credentials via STS.
Operational concerns: support for IP allowlist, predictable egress billing, transparent token-level cost breakdown, and route-based tracing hooks to tie requests to in-house observability.

POC plan & milestones: security questionnaire (complete) -> network topology workshop (3/12) -> pilot: 2-week load and integration test in eu-west-1 (target start 3/22) -> evaluate latency/cost/quality -> procurement SOW. Success criteria: p95 latency, throughput, KMS integration working, audit log delivery.
